{"metadata":{"description":"Encrypted credential vault for DeepSeek Harness — AES-256-GCM + TOTP, model tools + Settings UI","id":"gh:1333751043","install_available":true,"language":"TypeScript","name":"dsh-vault","slug":"Ox0400/dsh-vault","topics":["credentials","deepseek-harness","dsh-plugin","password-manager","totp","vault"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Encrypted credential vault for DeepSeek Harness — AES-256-GCM + TOTP, model tools + Settings UI"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-vault — Encrypted Credential Vault for DeepSeek Harness"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"**English** | 中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"dsh-vault is a security-focused plugin for DeepSeek Harness that stores sensitive credentials — **us"},{"id":"p4s2","text":"ernames, emails, phone numbers, passwords, TOTP secrets**, and developer credentials like **SSH conn"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"ections, API keys, secrets, and OAuth access/refresh tokens** — encrypted at rest, and exposes them "},{"id":"p4s4","text":"to the model through CRUD, search, password generation, and TOTP tools, plus a Settings UI page."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## Security & Implementation"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"- **Zero external crypto dependencies**: everything is built on Node's built-in `node:crypto` (AES-2"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"56-GCM authenticated encryption, scrypt key derivation, RFC 6238 TOTP).
- **Master password**: every"},{"id":"p6s3","text":" entry is encrypted with a 256-bit key derived via `scrypt(master password, salt)` and AES-256-GCM. "},{"id":"p6s4","text":"The key never touches disk; after unlock it is cached in-process and re-derived on restart.
- **Tamp"},{"id":"p6s5","text":"er-evident**: GCM auth tags plus a fixed-plaintext verification envelope — a wrong master password o"},{"id":"p6s6","text":"r modified ciphertext fails immediately, never returning garbage.
- **No plaintext at rest**: the on"},{"id":"p6s7","text":"-disk document contains no plaintext credentials; each entry uses an independent random nonce.
- **A"},{"id":"p6s8","text":"tomic writes**: reuses the harness `writeFileAtomic` + file lock; in-process writes are serialized, "},{"id":"p6s9","text":"cross-process writers take the lock.
- **Search never leaks**: `vault_search` returns summaries only"},{"id":"p6s10","text":" (id/title/kind/username/email/phone/host/port/url/tags) — **never passwords, keys, tokens, or TOTP "},{"id":"p6s11","text":"secrets**. Full credentials are readable only via explicit `vault_get` by id."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"### 1. What `env` is for"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"`get` fetches **one** value and needs no tag. `dsh-vault env` is for the other

tagged `env` as shell assignments, so th"},{"id":"p8s3","text":"e script picks them up itself:"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"`eval "$(dsh-vault env)"` reads those assignments into the **current shell** —
the usual reason to r"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"-vault env)"` reads those assignments into the **current shell** —
the usual reason to reach for it:"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"Two things worth knowing:"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"- **Only `env`-tagged entries are exported.** With none tagged you get
`dsh-vault: nothing to export"},{"id":"p13s2","text":" — no entry carries the "env" tag.`; tag one in the UI (the
entry's tags field) or with `vault_updat"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"e { id, tags: ["env"] }`.
- The name is derived from the title and field (`DASHSCOPE` + `apiKey` →
`"},{"id":"p13s4","text":"DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`) unless the entry sets `envKeys` — see
Environment export."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"**Names — there are only three, and two of them are the word `env` on purpose:**"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"| name | what it is | meaning |"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"| `env` | an entry **tag** | which entries `dsh-vault env` exports; nothing is exported without it |"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"
| `env` | the **command** | prints exactly the entries carrying that tag |
| `envKeys` | an entry *"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"*field** (optional) | pin exact names, e.g. `["DASHSCOPE_API_KEY"]`; the old singular `envKey` is ac"},{"id":"p16s4","text":"cepted as a one-element shorthand |"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"Nothing else is called `env*`: `list --json` / `show` report `envKeys` (the names
an entry exports —"},{"id":"p17s2","text":" what `get` accepts), `envTagged` (whether `env` includes it)
and `hasTotp` (whether `totp` can prod"},{"id":"p17s3","text":"), `envTagged` (whether `env` includes it)
and `hasTotp` (whether `totp` can produce a code for it)."},{"id":"p18s1","text":"## Privacy of the breach check"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"`vault_breach_check` (and the security page) can check passwords against Have I
Been Pwned. Exactly "},{"id":"p19s2","text":"one thing leaves this machine:"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"The response lists every suffix in that bucket (hundreds of hashes) and the match
is computed **loca"},{"id":"p21s2","text":"lly** — the full hash, the password, and the entry it belongs to
never leave. A password already in "},{"id":"p21s3","text":"the bundled common-password list is answered
offline and produces **no request at all**; repeat look"},{"id":"p21s4","text":"ups of the same prefix are
cached in memory for an hour."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"What k-anonymity does *not* hide, stated plainly:"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"- the **five-character prefix** (20 bits, one bucket in ~1M) goes to Cloudflare,
together with your "},{"id":"p23s2","text":"IP;
- an observer who can guess candidate passwords can compute each candidate's
prefix and see whet"},{"id":"p23s3","text":"her you queried that bucket — that is the known limit of
this protocol, not something the header fix"},{"id":"p23s4","text":"es;
- `Add-Padding` only removes the *response-size* signal (without it, a bucket's
response length "},{"id":"p23s5","text":"correlates with how common the password is)."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"To keep even the prefix on your machine, pass `online: false` — the check then
uses only the offline"},{"id":"p24s2","text":" list, which is far smaller, so treat it as a screening aid
rather than a verdict."},{"id":"p25s1","text":"## Security Boundaries & Known Limitations"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"### What this protects"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"- **A vault file that leaves the machine** — a backup, a synced folder, a stolen disk. Entries are A"},{"id":"p27s2","text":"ES-256-GCM encrypted under a key derived from the master password with scrypt (N=32768, r=8, p=1, pe"},{"id":"p27s3","text":"rsisted in the document and raisable later; old documents stay decryptable).
- **Other users on the "},{"id":"p27s4","text":"same machine** — the vault and every file the CLI writes are `0600`.
- **Secrets reaching the model'"},{"id":"p27s5","text":"s context by accident** — `vault_search` / `vault_update` never return passwords, keys or tokens, an"},{"id":"p27s6","text":"d the CLI exists so a script can read a secret without it passing through a conversation.
- **A pass"},{"id":"p27s7","text":"word embedded in config**, when you use `masterPasswordEnv` instead of `masterPassword` (see the war"},{"id":"p27s8","text":"d in config**, when you use `masterPasswordEnv` instead of `masterPassword` (see the warning above)."},{"id":"p28s1","text":"### What this does not protect"},{"id":"p29s1","text":"- **Another plugin in the same host process.** dsh-vault is itself a plugin: it runs in-process with"},{"id":"p29s2","text":" the harness and decrypted entries live in that process's memory. `readonly` / `ask` / `auto` constr"},{"id":"p29s3","text":"ain **the model's tool calls** — they do not isolate plugins from one another. The harness states th"},{"id":"p29s4","text":"e same limit for its own credential store: agent tool processes run as your OS user, so it "cannot i"},{"id":"p29s5","text":"solate secrets from the agent" (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials-local`). Only running plugins out-of-p"},{"id":"p29s6","text":"rocess would change this, and no plugin can enforce that by itself.
- **A compromised machine or use"},{"id":"p29s7","text":"r account** — a keylogger, a debugger attached to the harness process, or anything else running as y"},{"id":"p29s8","text":"ou.
- **A master password you typed into a file, a screenshot or a shell history.** Hence `masterPas"},{"id":"p29s9","text":"swordEnv`.
- **What the model does with a value you let it read.** `vault_get` returns it into that "},{"id":"p29s10","text":"tool call's result, which is model context; `vault_search`/`vault_update` never expose one."}],"truncated":true}
